description: An oscillator built from eight coupled limit-cycle systems that can be detuned, nudged by noise and driven by an external signal

params.text: Sets how much random noise is stirred into the eight systems, 0 to 1
Spreads the eight systems apart in frequency, 0 to 2
Sets how hard the external input drives the systems, 0 to 10
Picks one of twenty-one sets of frequency multipliers for the eight systems, from spread across five octaves below the note up to a harmonic series above it
Attenuates the voltage at the stochasticity jack before it is added to that knob, 0 to 2
Attenuates the voltage at the detune jack before it is added to that knob, 0 to 2
Attenuates the voltage at the external gain jack before it is added to that knob, 0 to 2
Attenuates the voltage at the harmonics jack before it is added to that knob, 0 to 2

inputs.text: Adds to the stochasticity knob through the small knob beside it
Adds to the detune knob through the small knob beside it
Adds to the external gain knob through the small knob beside it
Adds to the harmonics knob through the small knob beside it
Sets the pitch of the eight systems at a volt per octave, clamped to five octaves either side of C4
The signal driven into the eight systems, divided by ten before it reaches them

outputs.text: Carries the sum of the eight systems' x coordinates, clipped at 5V
Carries the sum of the eight systems' y coordinates, clipped at 5V

notes: with nothing patched and the stochasticity knob near zero the two outputs are close to sine waves a quarter cycle apart; noise and an external input make the shapes interesting
the four small knobs are attenuators for the jacks beside them and come up at 0.1, so a cable on its own has little effect until its small knob is raised
